context: Raincloud plot with 6 groups, each row showing a half-violin KDE, box plot, and jittered strip (~90 points/group); dual-encoded with 6 Tol colors and 6 distinct SVG patterns for accessibility; includes CVD deuteranopia simulation toggle
first_impression: Readable and well-organized — six rows are visually separated, the color palette is perceptually distinct, and the three-layer anatomy per row is consistently positioned so the eye knows where to look.
what_works: Dual color+pattern encoding is genuinely useful: the hatching on the violins makes Alpine (diagonal), Coastal (cross-hatch), and Fjord (vertical) distinguishable by texture alone, not just hue. Row separation and shared x-axis make cross-group median comparison fast.
what_doesnt: The anatomy legend uses near-identical blue circles for all three mark types (violin, box, strip), making it nearly useless for learning which layer is which — a tiny shape sample (curve, rect, dot) would communicate far better. The jittered strip at 90 points is near the density ceiling where overplotting starts to obscure distributional detail, especially for Boreal and Desert where the strip reads as a smear.
